sentences.show: In March 1944, 76 men crawled out of a Nazi prison camp, through a tunnel built from bed boards and tin cans. Only three made it home.
This is the real Great Escape. Stalag Luft III, a camp for captured airmen, built on sand, so nobody could tunnel out.
Even the huts stood on stilts, so guards could spot a tunnel.
But Squadron Leader Roger Bushell planned three tunnels. Tom, Dick and Harry. 600 men worked on them.
Nine metres down, barely wide enough for a man, held up with 4,000 boards stolen from their own beds.
Air came from a pump made of hockey sticks and milk tins. The sand went out in little bags, hidden inside their trousers.
On a moonless night, 24 March, they went through Harry.
One by one, 76 men crawled out into the forest. Then number 77 was spotted by a guard.
Hitler was furious. Fifty of them were shot by the Gestapo.
Only three reached freedom. Two Norwegians escaped to Sweden. A Dutch pilot made it to Spain.
Hollywood later filled the tunnel with Americans. Only one American really took part.
But the tunnel was real. Today, a line of stones in a Polish forest marks exactly where Harry ran.
Fifty men died for a few days of freedom. Was it worth it?
They dug for a year to get out. You only need one tap: subscribe.
